teamFindings.summary: VSiN 2.0 improves the DJ Moore camp outlook while retaining defensive-transition concern and flags Ty Johnson/C.J. Gardner-Johnson/Javon Solomon context. The post-cutdown roster/practice-squad sweep did not produce a separately governed point value.

VSiN 2.0 keeps the poor overall outlook but upgrades Malik Willis' camp evaluation and notes Malik Washington. Current NFL reporting has De'Von Achane back at practice with Tyreek Hill and Darren Waller on track for Week 1, which is useful availability context but not an approved numeric Walters calibration.

The Maye/A.J. Brown premise is retained by VSiN 2.0 while Will Campbell, the Kayshon Boutte trade and Christian Gonzalez status require current context. Boutte's move to Houston and Gonzalez's practice-injury recovery are confirmed current personnel facts; no governed point translation is available.

VSiN 2.0 preserves the bearish overall profile and supersedes the earlier Kenyon Sadiq readiness assumption while adding David Bailey/Breece Hall/OL context. The current roster cycle confirms Geno Smith's room and Cade Klubnik as QB2, but the guide's Sadiq health item was not given a new governed numeric value.

Danny Pinter's projected center role is definitively superseded by a torn patellar tendon and season-ending loss; VSiN also adds Ja'Kobi Lane development. This is material OL information, but the source-locked package requires replacement-aware calibrated values before a point move.

VSiN 2.0 retains the elite-offense/below-average-defense construction and adds Ja'Marr Chase knee, DJ Turner/Cashius Howell and Dohnte Meyers context. Current cutdown activity does not supply an approved replacement-value or rating delta.

The quarterback competition is resolved: Deshaun Watson is the Week 1 starter, consistent with VSiN 2.0's supersession, while the pessimistic offensive premise remains. Existing matchup-specific re-entry uncertainty is preserved; no additional rating point was invented.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Rodgers/McCarthy thesis but increases OL concern and identifies Broderick Jones' departure and Drew Allar development. Post-cutdown quarterback/roster shape is current context only; no approved numeric Walters calibration maps it to a carried-rating delta.

Jayden Higgins' torn ACL is confirmed and Kayshon Boutte's acquisition materially changes the receiver room; current NFL reporting also expects C.J. Gardner-Johnson ready for Week 1. The facts are material, but no source-locked player/replacement-value release supports a numeric rating move today.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Daniel Jones baseline and adds Riley Leonard QB2, Keenan Allen and receiver-health context. Current reporting keeps Allen in the Week 1 plan and the post-cutdown depth chart is stable enough for monitoring, not an uncalibrated point adjustment.

VSiN 2.0 clarifies Travis Hunter as a starting corner/defense-first player with occasional receiver work. The roster review provides no contrary current fact and no governed numeric role value, so the carried rating remains unchanged.
VSiN 2.0 retains Cam Ward/Saleh/Daboll optimism, adds OL downside and Elic Ayomanor development. Cutdown/depth changes were reviewed with no approved point-equivalent calibration for a rating move.

VSiN 2.0 supersedes Bo Nix recovery uncertainty with a healthy/sharp post-preseason status and retains the elite-defense premise. Jonathon Cooper's Week 1 unavailability was already confirmed in the prior review; no new source-locked numeric adjustment is supported.

VSiN 2.0 improves Mahomes health versus the earlier uncertainty and adds offensive/roster context. Current reporting continues to target Week 1 with rehabilitation progressing, while the prior review retained final-clearance monitoring; no unapproved QB point move was applied.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Cousins bridge/Mendoza development plan and adds Ashton Jeanty/Hezekiah Masses context. The current post-cutdown QB/depth cycle was reviewed; no source-locked player-value release converts it into a rating move.

Tyler Biadasz's projected OL upgrade is definitively superseded by season-ending knee/ACL injured reserve, with rookie Jake Slaughter next at center. The current ledger already contains a carried LAC downgrade from the initial sweep; Tuesday adds no second uncalibrated penalty and avoids double counting.

VSiN 2.0 improves Tyler Guyton LT uncertainty and adds encouraging defensive-camp and veteran context. Current reporting lists Guyton as a full practice participant; this confirms availability direction but does not create a governed numeric delta.

VSiN 2.0 reinforces the Harbaugh culture/defense thesis while flagging offensive messaging around Jaxson Dart. Odell Beckham made the 53-man roster and current depth/returner availability was reviewed; no governed point move is supported.
VSiN 2.0 downgrades the earlier Sean Mannion offensive optimism while retaining defensive strength. The cutdown/practice-squad review yielded no new point-equivalent fact approved for BW FAIR.

VSiN 2.0 retains Daniels/coordinator rebound context but flags season-impacting losses at LT/DT. Those losses were already incorporated into the carried state by the initial research delta; Tuesday avoids a duplicate penalty and preserves the existing rating pending approved replacement-value calibration.

VSiN 2.0 retains turnover-regression concern and adds LT/secondary health risk. Current roster/depth review does not provide an approved numeric loss relative to replacement, so no point move is made.

VSiN 2.0 says the existing OL/health concerns worsened, including Cade Mays and secondary/skill-position health. The current cutdown state was reviewed, but no approved position-cluster calibration exists to turn this into a new point delta.

Josh Jacobs' commissioner-exempt status is confirmed and Green Bay added backfield depth. VSiN also flags a severe Micah Parsons availability downgrade; current official reporting independently establishes that Parsons opens on PUP and misses at least four games, while the exact guide injury wording is not needed for the availability conclusion. The existing GB carried downgrade is preserved without stacking an uncalibrated second move.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Kyler Murray/O'Connell reclamation thesis and adds secondary/Jordan Mason context. Minnesota kept J.J. McCarthy on the initial roster behind Murray, confirming the starter hierarchy without supplying a new governed point value.

Jalon Walker's season-ending ACL loss is independently confirmed and the Week 1 quarterback question remains material. Atlanta already carries a defensive-front downgrade and a matchup-specific QB uncertainty adjustment from the initial build; Tuesday does not double count either condition.

VSiN 2.0 reinforces the bearish camp/OL/defensive-loss picture. Current reporting adds Jalen Coker to IR, Brady Christensen to IR and Ikem Ekwonu day-to-day, reinforcing uncertainty but still lacking an approved cluster/replacement numeric calibration.

VSiN 2.0 weakens the offensive setup; Jordyn Tyson's roughly two-month hamstring absence is independently confirmed. New Orleans already carries a trench downgrade from the initial sweep, and no source-locked skill-player replacement value exists to justify stacking another numeric move.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Bucky Irving/offensive premise and describes a comparatively clean camp with new defensive health context. Jalon Daniels earned QB2 behind Baker Mayfield; no material starter or unit change clears the governed numeric threshold.

VSiN 2.0 retains weak-QB/team context and flags Jeremiyah Love plus OL injuries. Current reporting says Love is progressing well toward Week 1 and Carson Beck is full-go in practice; the changing availability state argues for monitoring rather than an uncalibrated static point deduction.

Aaron Donald's possible comeback has become an actual return, but current participation remains a separate question; VSiN also flags health/availability counterweights. Because Walters requires player and replacement values rather than reputation adjustments, Donald's return is a mandatory matchup revalidation item, not an invented rating bump.

The earlier healthier-roster premise is superseded. Ricky Pearsall's season-ending knee surgery is confirmed; Nick Bosa remains in return-to-practice monitoring. The receiver loss is material, but the package has no approved current player/replacement-value release for a numeric rating delta.

VSiN 2.0 retains the Darnold/Price/JSN structure and increases uncertainty around Zach Charbonnet and the defensive backfield. The official Week 1 schedule preview likewise identifies Charbonnet recovery and a changed backfield/defensive depth picture. No approved numeric personnel calibration supports a new rating move.
